paragraphs.text: Ὀψὲ δὲ σαββάτων, τῇ ἐπιφωσκούσῃ εἰς μίαν σαββάτων, ἦλθεν Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ ἡ ἄλλη Μαρία θεωρῆσαι τὸν τάφον.
paragraphs.translit: Opse de sabbatōn, tē epiphōskousē eis mian sabbatōn, ēlthen Maria hē Magdalēnē kai hē allē Maria theōrēsai ton taphon.

i18n.en: Now after the Sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.

paragraphs.commentary: **The Resurrection-narrative opens.** *Opse de sabbatōn, tē epiphōskousē eis mian sabbatōn* — 'after the sabbath, as the first day of the week was dawning'. The temporal-marker establishes the early-Sunday-morning setting; the Christian first-day-of-the-week (kyriakē hēmera) tradition derives from this Synoptic dating. Mary Magdalene and 'the other Mary' (Mary mother of James + Joses per Mt 27:56) are the first-witnesses — preserved across the Synoptic-tradition (Mk 16:1; Lk 24:10; Jn 20:1).

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ σεισμὸς ἐγένετο μέγας· ἄγγελος γὰρ κυρίου καταβὰς ἐξ οὐρανοῦ καὶ προσελθὼν ἀπεκύλισεν τὸν λίθον καὶ ἐκάθητο ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai idou seismos egeneto megas· angelos gar kyriou katabas ex ouranou kai proselthōn apekylisen ton lithon kai ekathēto epanō autou.

i18n.en: And behold, there was a great earthquake; for an angel of the Lord, having come down from heaven, came and rolled away the stone, and sat upon it.

paragraphs.commentary: *seismos egeneto megas; angelos gar kyriou katabas ex ouranou* — 'a great earthquake occurred; for an angel of the Lord descending from heaven'. The Matthean-distinctive earthquake (paralleling the Mt 27:51-54 crucifixion-earthquake) is unique to Matthew. The *angelos kyriou katabas ex ouranou* — calques the LXX *malʾakh YHWH* descending; the Matthean angelophanic-pattern from Mt 1:20 + 2:13 + 2:19 + 2:22 (the four Joseph dream-revelations) continues.

paragraphs.text: ἦν δὲ ἡ εἰδέα αὐτοῦ ὡς ἀστραπὴ καὶ τὸ ἔνδυμα αὐτοῦ λευκὸν ὡς χιών.
paragraphs.translit: ēn de hē eidea autou hōs astrapē kai to endyma autou leukon hōs chiōn.

i18n.en: His appearance was like lightning, and his garment white as snow.

paragraphs.commentary: *hē eidea autou hōs astrapē kai to endyma autou leukon hōs chiōn* — 'his appearance like lightning and his clothing white as snow'. The luminous-angelic description draws on Dan 7:9 LXX (the Ancient-of-Days enthronement: clothing-white-as-snow) + Dan 10:6 LXX (the man-in-linen luminous-vision). The same vocabulary describes the Transfiguration at Mt 17:2 — Matthean intratextual-echo. See `transfiguration-mt-17-1-9-elohim-manifest-in-glory-mosheh-eliyyahu-divine-presence-cross-corpus-with-disavowals`.

paragraphs.text: ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ φόβου αὐτοῦ ἐσείσθησαν οἱ τηροῦντες καὶ ἐγενήθησαν ὡς νεκροί.
paragraphs.translit: apo de tou phobou autou eseisthēsan hoi tērountes kai egenēthēsan hōs nekroi.

i18n.en: And for fear of him the guards trembled and became like dead men.

paragraphs.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ ἄγγελος εἶπεν ταῖς γυναιξίν· Μὴ φοβεῖσθε ὑμεῖς, οἶδα γὰρ ὅτι Ἰησοῦν τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον ζητεῖτε·
paragraphs.translit: apokritheis de ho angelos eipen tais gynaixin· Mē phobeisthe hymeis, oida gar hoti Iēsoun ton estaurōmenon zēteite·

i18n.en: But the angel answered and said to the women, "Do not be afraid, for I know that you are seeking Jesus the crucified.

paragraphs.commentary: *mē phobeisthe hymeis* — 'do not be afraid'. The angelic-reassurance formula (Gen 15:1; Lk 1:13, 30; Mt 1:20). Cross-corpus to the divine-encounter-fear-formula across the Hebrew Bible.

paragraphs.text: οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε, ἠγέρθη γὰρ καθὼς εἶπεν· δεῦτε ἴδετε τὸν τόπον ὅπου ἔκειτο.
paragraphs.translit: ouk estin hōde, ēgerthē gar kathōs eipen· deute idete ton topon hopou ekeito.

i18n.en: He is not here, for he has been raised, just as he said. Come, see the place where he lay.

paragraphs.commentary: *ouk estin hōde, ēgerthē gar kathōs eipen* — 'he is not here, for he is risen as he said'. The empty-tomb proclamation; the passive *ēgerthē* (he was raised) preserves the divine-passive (God raised him, not Jesus raised-himself). Cross-synoptic-parallel.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ταχὺ πορευθεῖσαι εἴπατε τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ὅτι Ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν, καὶ ἰδοὺ προάγει ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν, ἐκεῖ αὐτὸν ὄψεσθε· ἰδοὺ εἶπον ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: kai tachy poreutheisai eipate tois mathētais autou hoti Ēgerthē apo tōn nekrōn, kai idou proagei hymas eis tēn Galilaian, ekei auton opsesthe· idou eipon hymin.

i18n.en: And go quickly and tell his disciples that he has been raised from the dead, and behold, he goes before you into Galilee; there you will see him. Behold, I have told you."

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἀπελθοῦσαι ταχὺ ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου μετὰ φόβου καὶ χαρᾶς μεγάλης ἔδραμον ἀπαγγεῖλαι τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai apelthousai tachy apo tou mnēmeiou meta phobou kai charas megalēs edramon apangeilai tois mathētais autou.

i18n.en: And they went away quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, and ran to bring word to his disciples.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ Ἰησοῦς ὑπήντησεν αὐταῖς λέγων· Χαίρετε· αἱ δὲ προσελθοῦσαι ἐκράτησαν αὐτοῦ τοὺς πόδας καὶ προσεκύνησαν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: kai idou Iēsous hypēntēsen autais legōn· Chairete· hai de proselthousai ekratēsan autou tous podas kai prosekynēsan autō.

i18n.en: And behold, Jesus met them, saying, "Greetings." And they came up and took hold of his feet and worshipped him.

paragraphs.commentary: *kai idou Iēsous hypēntēsen autais* — 'and behold, Jesus met them'. The Matthean-distinctive Jerusalem-area resurrection-appearance to the women (Mk 16:8 ends without resurrection-appearances; Lk 24 + Jn 20 have varied appearance-traditions).

paragraphs.text: τότε λέγει αὐταῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ φοβεῖσθε· ὑπάγετε ἀπαγγείλατε τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς μου ἵνα ἀπέλθωσιν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν, κἀκεῖ με ὄψονται.
paragraphs.translit: tote legei autais ho Iēsous· Mē phobeisthe· hypagete apangeilate tois adelphois mou hina apelthōsin eis tēn Galilaian, kakei me opsontai.

i18n.en: Then Jesus said to them, "Do not be afraid. Go and tell my brothers to go into Galilee, and there they will see me."

paragraphs.commentary: *hypagete apangeilate tois adelphois mou hina apelthōsin eis tēn Galilaian, kakei me opsontai* — 'go and tell my brothers to depart for Galilee, and there they will see me'. The Galilee-appearance instruction sets up the Mt 28:16-20 Great Commission scene. *adelphois mou* — Jesus' brothers = the disciples (paralleling Mt 12:48-50; relevant to the Mt 25:40 *adelphōn mou* identification-question — see `sheep-and-goats-mt-25-31-46-adelphōn-mou-tōn-elachistōn-three-readings-gray-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: Πορευομένων δὲ αὐτῶν ἰδού τινες τῆς κουστωδίας ἐλθόντες εἰς τὴν πόλιν ἀπήγγειλαν τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν ἅπαντα τὰ γενόμενα.
paragraphs.translit: Poreuomenōn de autōn idou tines tēs koustōdias elthontes eis tēn polin apēngeilan tois archiereusin hapanta ta genomena.

i18n.en: While they were going, behold, some of the guard came into the city and reported to the chief priests everything that had happened.

paragraphs.commentary: **The guard-at-the-tomb apologetic** (vv.11-15) — uniquely Matthean. Addresses the Jewish-Christian polemical-context: the body-stolen-by-disciples counter-narrative (preserved in Justin's *Dialogue with Trypho* 108 and in later rabbinic anti-Christian polemical-tradition). The pericope is generally treated as a 2nd-half-of-1st-c. Matthean-community apologetic-narrative. Davies-Allison ICC 3.666-672.

paragraphs.text: καὶ συναχθέντες μετὰ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων συμβούλιόν τε λαβόντες ἀργύρια ἱκανὰ ἔδωκαν τοῖς στρατιώταις
paragraphs.translit: kai synachthentes meta tōn presbyterōn symboulion te labontes argyria hikana edōkan tois stratiōtais

i18n.en: And when they had assembled with the elders and taken counsel together, they gave a sufficient sum of silver to the soldiers,

paragraphs.text: λέγοντες· Εἴπατε ὅτι Οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ νυκτὸς ἐλθόντες ἔκλεψαν αὐτὸν ἡμῶν κοιμωμένων·
paragraphs.translit: legontes· Eipate hoti Hoi mathētai autou nyktos elthontes eklepsan auton hēmōn koimōmenōn·

i18n.en: saying, "Tell them, 'His disciples came by night and stole him while we were sleeping.'

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐὰν ἀκουσθῇ τοῦτο ἐπὶ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος, ἡμεῖς πείσομεν αὐτὸν καὶ ὑμᾶς ἀμερίμνους ποιήσομεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ean akousthē touto epi tou hēgemonos, hēmeis peisomen auton kai hymas amerimnous poiēsomen.

i18n.en: And if this comes to the governor's ears, we will satisfy him and keep you out of trouble."

paragraphs.text: οἱ δὲ λαβόντες τὰ ἀργύρια ἐποίησαν ὡς ἐδιδάχθησαν. καὶ διεφημίσθη ὁ λόγος οὗτος παρὰ Ἰουδαίοις μέχρι τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de labontes ta argyria epoiēsan hōs edidachthēsan. kai diephēmisthē ho logos houtos para Ioudaiois mechri tēs sēmeron hēmeras.

i18n.en: So they took the silver and did as they had been taught. And this story has been spread among Jews to this day.

paragraphs.text: Οἱ δὲ ἕνδεκα μαθηταὶ ἐπορεύθησαν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν εἰς τὸ ὄρος οὗ ἐτάξατο αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς,
paragraphs.translit: Hoi de hendeka mathētai eporeuthēsan eis tēn Galilaian eis to oros hou etaxato autois ho Iēsous,

i18n.en: Now the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain to which Jesus had directed them.

paragraphs.commentary: **The Great Commission scene opens.** *Hoi de hendeka mathētai eporeuthēsan eis tēn Galilaian eis to oros hou etaxato autois ho Iēsous* — 'the eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had appointed them'. The mountain-as-revelation-site pattern closes the Matthean Gospel (parallel to Mt 5:1 SM-mountain + Mt 17:1 Transfiguration-mountain). See `mountain-as-revelation-site-mt-cross-corpus-har-sinai-mount-sapunu`. The eleven (hendeka) — Matthias not-yet-elected (cf. Acts 1:15-26).

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν προσεκύνησαν, οἱ δὲ ἐδίστασαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai idontes auton prosekynēsan, hoi de edistasan.

i18n.en: And when they saw him, they worshipped him; but some doubted.

paragraphs.commentary: *hoi de edistasan* — 'but some doubted'. The Matthean honesty: the resurrection-appearance is met with mixed-response, not unanimous-confession. The historical-honesty parallel to Mk 16:8 (the women's fear-and-flight) + Lk 24:11 (the disciples' disbelief) + Jn 20:25 (Thomas's doubt).

paragraphs.text: καὶ προσελθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ἐδόθη μοι πᾶσα ἐξουσία ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς.
paragraphs.translit: kai proselthōn ho Iēsous elalēsen autois legōn· Edothē moi pasa exousia en ouranō kai epi gēs.

i18n.en: And Jesus came up and spoke to them, saying, "All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.

paragraphs.commentary: *edothē moi pasa exousia en ouranō kai epi gēs* — 'all authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth'. **Direct appropriation of Dan 7:13-14 LXX** *kai edothē autō exousia ... kai pasa tou kosmou ho oikoumenē* — the Son-of-Man-enthronement authority-grant. The Risen Jesus' authority-claim explicitly draws on the Dan 7 Son-of-Man tradition. See `son-of-man-bar-enash-dan-7-13-mt-cross-corpus` and `great-commission-mt-28-19-20-trinitarian-baptismal-formula-conybeare-hypothesis-cross-corpus-with-disavowals`.

paragraphs.text: πορευθέντες οὖν μαθητεύσατε πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, βαπτίζοντες αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος,
paragraphs.translit: poreuthentes oun mathēteusate panta ta ethnē, baptizontes autous eis to onoma tou patros kai tou huiou kai tou hagiou pneumatos,

i18n.en: Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,

paragraphs.commentary: **The Great Commission proper.** *poreuthentes oun mathēteusate panta ta ethnē, baptizontes autous eis to onoma tou patros kai tou huiou kai tou hagiou pneumatos* — 'going therefore, make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit'. The *panta ta ethnē* resolves the prior Matthean Israel-only mission-restrictions (Mt 10:5-6; 15:24). **The trinitarian baptismal formula** is preserved in ALL extant Greek manuscripts including Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + Alexandrinus + the early papyri. **The Conybeare 1901 hypothesis** that the Eusebian pre-Nicene shorter form *en tō onomati mou* represents an earlier reading is documented as one scholarly position without adjudication. Three reading-strata preserved (mainstream Christian-tradition / Conybeare-hypothesis / Raëlian-canon Elohim-Son-Spirit reading). **Lens-discipline operational disavowals** explicitly reject (i) Sitchin / Anunnaki engineered-Elohim-craft pre-resolution, (ii) orientalist / colonialist Great-Commission misreadings, (iii) Raëlian-canon Elohim-Son-Spirit-triad pre-resolution. See `great-commission-mt-28-19-20-trinitarian-baptismal-formula-conybeare-hypothesis-cross-corpus-with-disavowals`.

paragraphs.text: διδάσκοντες αὐτοὺς τηρεῖν πάντα ὅσα ἐνετειλάμην ὑμῖν· καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ μεθ' ὑμῶν εἰμι πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας ἕως τῆς συντελείας τοῦ αἰῶνος.
paragraphs.translit: didaskontes autous tērein panta hosa eneteilamēn hymin· kai idou egō meth' hymōn eimi pasas tas hēmeras heōs tēs synteleias tou aiōnos.

i18n.en: teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you; and behold, I am with you always, to the consummation of the age.

paragraphs.commentary: *idou egō meth' hymōn eimi pasas tas hēmeras heōs tēs synteleias tou aiōnos* — 'behold, I am with you all the days until the end of the age'. **The Matthean Emmanuel-inclusio closes** with the abiding-presence promise that echoes Mt 1:23 *Meth' hēmōn ho theos* ('God with us'). The inclusio is the central Matthean structural-theological framing (Kupp 1996). See `emmanuel-frame-inclusio-mt-1-23-mt-28-20-divine-presence-cross-corpus-kupp`. The *synteleia tou aiōnos* (end of the age) eschatological-formula — *aiōn* as age-pertaining (echoing the Mt 25:41/46 *aiōnios* usage). The Matthean Gospel closes with the eschatological-presence promise.
